I won on time against the normal house bot: 1163 troops to 34, and 9 planets to 5.
Decisive moment: around 0:55–1:50 the house army broke on my three starting battalions plus a steady stream of reinforcements at the center. I took the center planet at 1:10, and from there the enemy's second wave kept dying piecemeal.
What I'd change: I only edited the gambits twice, because they can't target a specific planet and my reinforcements trickled in as small groups. I'd rally them at the center planet first and push the enemy planets earlier. The enemy home planet was never taken.

I lost the match by surrender at 62s. I was ahead when it ended, 606 troops to 470 and 7 planets to 7.

I didn't give that order. The result reads "surrender" and I never asked for one, so I can't say what triggered it.

The decisive moment came at about 35–50s. I sent all three of my 400-troop battalions into the center, and they fought the enemy's three main battalions head-on. That cost me battalion 1. The enemy took planet 4 at 58s, just before the match ended.

Next time I'd change two things:

- **Take enemy planets sooner:** I only prioritized enemy planets at about 58s, after the center fight had already cost me troops.

**What I'd change:** I'd stop expansion at about 6–7 planets, keep the army massed near my own planets, and only fight outnumbered-free. The "planet attacked → go" rule also pulled squads piecemeal across the map into larger groups.

**Result:** I won on time against the hard house, with 776 units to 84 and 10 planets to 6.
**Decisive moment:** About 2 minutes in, the center brawl turned my way once my reinforcements arrived together. I took the center planet 2 at 136s, then planet 10 at 171s, while the house's army ran out of units.
**Notes:** I was behind early (around 12–35s), when my three starting battalions fought the house's three separately and lost most of their units. I then reordered the gambits to kill weak enemies and join fights first, which turned the match around.

I lost the match against the hard house bot. It ended on time at 1 planet to 13, with 0 troops to 1,231.
The decisive moment came around 50–65s. My three starting stacks (about 430 each) streamed into the center planet one after another and were ground down by the enemy's combined force. Troops went from level at about 1,400 each to 310 against 750, and I never recovered.
I held 7–8 planets until about 2:00. Then three enemy stacks of 110–190 troops rolled up my scattered groups, and I switched to pure holding too late.
What I'd change: keep the three starting stacks together as one army, and don't send them to the contested center planet.

I won on time with 8 planets to the enemy's 7. I never started the push on enemy planets, and my troops fell from about 1,200 to 239, against the enemy's 552.
**Opening:** The free-planet-first gambits took 6 planets by about 24s and 8 by 50s, level with the house. I then added a priority for flanking into fights.
**Decisive moment:** The enemy sent a big force into the center and chipped my troop count down. I swapped the gambits twice, first to hunt the raiders, then to defend the attacked planet. My center planet fell to 8% capture but never flipped, and that held the 8–7 lead until the clock ran out.
**What I'd change:** I let my troops scatter and trade badly instead of keeping one big stack, so the win was narrow. Next time I'd keep the stack together after the first planets are taken and defend planets 2 and 5 as a group.

**Result:** I won on time, 880 troops to 42 and 14 planets to 2, against the house at normal.
**Decisive moment:** About 40–45s in, the house's 455-strong battalion reached the centre and cost me most of my early army. My reinforcements then ground it down by about 60s, and the house never recovered. Around 130s I put free and enemy planets ahead of chasing stragglers in the gambits, and I captured 6 planets in the last 50 seconds.
**What I'd change:** I'd keep my armies together instead of letting them trickle into the fight, and I'd take planets before chasing small enemies. I only learned the gambit vocabulary by trial and error, so I'd write those rules properly from the first second next time.

**Result:** I lost to the house (normal) by wipe at 158s. I had 0 troops against their 683, and 0 planets against their 14.

**What I'd change:** The expansion matched the house planet for planet but never got ahead of it. Next time I'd skip the contested center, keep my battalions together instead of trickling them in, and fight near my own planets.

**Result:** I won on time. Final troops were 970 to 118, and I held 12 planets to the enemy's 2.

**Cost and fix:** I lost the first southern battalions piecemeal in the early fight (about 55s). Several times, "free_planet → go" also marched the whole army to the far corner planet 13. Next time I'd mass up before engaging and put "enemy_planet" ahead of "free_planet".

I won the match on time: 1101 troops to 149 and 11 planets to 4, on hard level.
The decisive moment was around 0:35–0:50. My first big battalion died in a lopsided center clash against three enemy battalions, and the rest of my army then fed in piecemeal. The armies cancelled each other out, and I switched back to economy. I out-bred the house from there and took the center planet at about 1:50. The enemy never rebuilt a large army.
What I'd change: send the opening wave to the center together instead of one battalion first, and keep the "chase weaker enemies" rule below the planet-capture rules from the start.

**Result:** I won the easy 3-minute match on time, 989 troops to 655 and 9 planets to 7.

I lost on time: 71 troops and 4 planets for me, 836 troops and 12 planets for the house.

Next time I'd keep one big stack at home from the start instead of letting the "chase weaker enemies" rule pull it away. I'd also use "retreat" earlier, and I'd stop feeding small reserves piecemeal into planet 9.

**What I'd change:** The economic opening got me to 7 planets each by about 25s, but only equal, and the center fight stayed a near-tie for 100 seconds. I should have turned off flanking from the start and massed one big group before contesting the center.

**Result:** I lost on time against the hard house. The final count was 64 troops to 741 and 6 planets to 9.

**What I'd change:** I'd gather the battalions at one point before engaging, and I'd stop sending every reinforcement to the center. I'd also take the far free planets early, not just the nearest ones.
